covers: The command fields of two bytes of the Zilog SCC: WR0 (CRC reset code in bits 7-6, keyed by the byte itself, 0x00 to 0xFF; command in bits 5-3, keyed 0x100 plus the field in place) and WR9 (reset command in bits 7-6, keyed 0x200 plus the byte). A single byte can carry a CRC code and a command together

entries.name: CRC reset null
entries.description: WR0 bits 7-6 are 00: no CRC reset.
entries.behaviour: Keyed by the byte written to WR0, whose bits 7-6 select the CRC reset code. No action; the pointer and command fields of the same byte still apply.

entries.name: reset Rx CRC checker
entries.description: WR0 bits 7-6 are 01: reset the receive CRC checker.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: MAME only logs it. The pointer and command fields of the same byte still apply.

entries.name: reset Tx underrun latch
entries.description: WR0 bits 7-6 are 11: reset the transmit underrun/EOM latch.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: MAME only logs it, and RR0 bit 6 is not changed. The pointer and command fields of the same byte still apply.

entries.name: null command
entries.behaviour: Bits 5-3 of the WR0 byte are 000. No action; the pointer and CRC reset fields of the same byte still apply.

entries.name: point high
entries.description: WR0 command 1: the next control access reaches registers 8 to 15.
entries.behaviour: On Z85X3X types it adds 8 to the register pointer in bits 2-0 of the same byte, for one access. On Z80X30 types it is a null command.

entries.name: reset ext/status ints
entries.description: WR0 command 2: release the latched RR0 status and the external interrupt.
entries.behaviour: Clears the channel's pending external interrupt and the RR0 latch, but only when no WR15-enabled status bit differs now from the latched value; otherwise the latch and the interrupt stay.

entries.name: send abort
entries.description: WR0 command 3: send an SDLC abort.
entries.behaviour: Not implemented: MAME only logs it and the transmitter is not flushed.

entries.name: enable int on next Rx
entries.description: WR0 command 4: arm the first-character receive interrupt again.
entries.behaviour: Sets the flag that lets WR1 mode 01 (interrupt on the first character) interrupt on the next character received.

entries.name: reset Tx int pending
entries.description: WR0 command 5: clear a pending transmit interrupt.
entries.behaviour: Clears the channel's pending transmit interrupt and its RR3 bit, and suppresses the interrupt that the character now being sent would raise when it completes.

entries.name: error reset
entries.description: WR0 command 6: unlock the receive FIFO after an error.
entries.behaviour: When the receive FIFO is not empty it steps past the character at its head, which is lost if unread, and so ends the lock a special condition set.

entries.name: reset highest IUS
entries.description: WR0 command 7: end service of the highest-priority interrupt.
entries.behaviour: Clears the first in-service flag in the order A external/special, A transmit, A receive, B external/special, B transmit, B receive, updates the interrupt line, then re-checks the receive interrupt condition.

entries.name: no reset
entries.behaviour: Keyed 0x200 plus the byte written to WR9, whose bits 7-6 are the reset command. The other WR9 bits are stored and nothing is reset.

entries.name: reset channel B
entries.description: WR9 bits 7-6 are 01: channel reset of channel B.
entries.behaviour: Empties the FIFOs, sets WR0 and WR5 to 0, WR4 to 0x04, WR15 to 0xF8, keeps WR1 bits 2 and 5 and WR3 bit 0, and sets RR0 bits 2 and 6. Stops the baud timer and recomputes /RTS and /DTR; pending interrupt state is not cleared.

entries.name: reset channel A
entries.description: WR9 bits 7-6 are 10: channel reset of channel A.
entries.behaviour: The same channel reset for channel A, which also clears the pending and in-service state of every interrupt source of both channels.

entries.name: hardware reset
entries.description: WR9 bits 7-6 are 11: reset the whole device.
entries.behaviour: Resets both channels and gives WR10 0, WR11 0x08 and WR14 bits 5-4 set; Z80X30 types keep WR0 bits 1-0. WR9 keeps bits 3, 4 and 2 as written (interrupt enable, status high, disable lower chain) and clears bits 0, 1 and 5.
